record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: If one is given only random sample points rather than oracle access, can the volume of a polytope with a bounded number of facets be computed efficiently from that sample? The paper poses this as the remaining positive case after noting a superpolynomial lower bound for general convex bodies.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, it remains open to efficiently compute the volume from a random sample for polytopes with a bounded number of facets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and let $m=m(d)$ be a function bounded by a fixed polynomial in $d$ (so we consider polytopes with at most polynomially many facets). Suppose $P\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is an unknown convex polytope defined as the intersection of at most $m$ closed half-spaces, and suppose the only access to $P$ is through a sample of points $X_1,\dots,X_N$ drawn i.i.d. from the uniform distribution on $P$ (no membership oracle, no separation oracle, and no explicit list of the facets is given).

Question: Does there exist a randomized algorithm which, given $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$ and a sample of size $N=\mathrm{poly}(d,m,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ from the uniform distribution on $P$, runs in time polynomial in $d$, $m$, $1/\varepsilon$, and $\log(1/\delta)$, and outputs a number $V$ satisfying
$$ (1-\varepsilon)\,\mathrm{vol}(P)\;\le\;V\;\le\;(1+\varepsilon)\,\mathrm{vol}(P) $$
with probability at least $1-\delta$?

Equivalently: can the volume of a polytope with a polynomially bounded number of facets be approximated efficiently from random samples alone? It is known that for general convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^d$ accessed only through random samples a superpolynomial number of samples is required, so the question is whether the polytopal case with few facets escapes this lower bound.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution. Standard polytope volume algorithms assume oracle access (membership/separation), and recent work on volume approximation via random walks still presupposes such oracles. Sample-only volume estimation has known superpolynomial lower bounds for general convex bodies, but no clear positive or negative result was located for polytopes with a bounded number of facets.

status_evidence.title: Convex volume approximation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Randomized polynomial time approximation scheme by Dyer, Frieze, and Kannan uses oracle access to the convex body.
status_evidence.claim: Existing FPRAS-type results assume oracle access, not random sample access.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Random-Walk Methods for Approximating Polytope Volume
status_evidence.snippet: Practical algorithms for polytope volume rely on random walks from a known H-representation of the polytope.
status_evidence.claim: Recent volume algorithms still require an explicit description of facets, not pure sample access.

status_evidence.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Learning High-dimensional Simplices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sample complexity for learning simplices from samples; theoretical aspects still contain open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Sample-based learning/volume questions for polytopes with few facets remain partly open.
